chunks: And the confirmation of that is what was narrated by Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him:
That he was asked about a man who dies while having no heir and no ʿaṣabah. He said: “He may bequeath his wealth wherever he wishes among the Muslims, the poor, and the wayfarer.”

key_terms.عَصَبَةَ: agnatic male relatives who inherit through the paternal line
key_terms.وَارِثَ: an heir entitled to inherit the estate
key_terms.يُوصِي بِمَالِهِ: he makes a bequest concerning his property

ai.seo_question: What may a person without heirs do with his wealth before death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who dies without an heir or agnatic male relatives. It states that such a person may direct his wealth by bequest as he wishes among the Muslims, the poor, and the wayfarer.
